# Report usage across every tool round, not just the last

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#93
Labels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:S, area:api

## Why

`afterModelResponse` is the hook a deployer reaches for when they need to record what a turn cost — an audit entry, a billing line, a usage budget. It is called once per user message, after the round loop exits, and is handed the `lastUsage` local: `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone.

For a turn that answered directly, that is the whole turn. For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere. A deployer billing or budgeting from this hook under-counts exactly the expensive turns, and nothing in the signature hints at it. The current behaviour is recorded in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` so it is at least discoverable, but documenting a surprising number is weaker than not producing one.

Raised by the reviewer on HALEngine#83, which recorded the behaviour but could not change it: that PR's ticket scoped itself to specifying the seam, not altering the orchestrator.

## What to do

Decide, and make the signature say the answer. Two shapes are worth weighing, and the issue should record why the other was rejected:

- Accumulate across rounds and pass the sum, keeping one `usage` argument. Simple for the common case, and it silently changes what an existing consumer records — the number gets larger for tool-heavy turns, which is the point, but it is a behaviour change worth a MINOR bump and a changelog line that says so.
- Pass both, for example the summed total plus the per-round breakdown, so a consumer that wants provider-call granularity keeps it. More faithful, wider surface.

Whichever is chosen, a turn that ran no tools must report exactly what it reports today, so the common path does not move.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A turn driven through two tool rounds reports usage covering every provider call in that turn, asserted against a scripted provider whose rounds report known, different token counts
- [ ] A turn with no tool calls reports exactly what it reports today, pinned by the existing test remaining unedited
- [ ] A provider that reports no usage on some rounds does not make the total `undefined` or `NaN`: the rounds that reported are still counted, and a turn where nothing reported still reports nothing
- [ ] The type of what the hook receives makes the answer unambiguous, so a reader does not have to open the orchestrator to learn whether it is a sum
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded under-counting line with the new behaviour, and the CHANGELOG entry states the change in what an existing consumer will record
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the public API

## Tech notes

Out of scope: the audit entry or billing record itself, which is a consumer's concern; token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes; and the `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate and this issue only aggregates.

Key files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `lastUsage` local and the `afterModelResponse` call site), `src/types/ai.ts` (`UsageMetadata`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.

specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:26:- Creating a chat is refused `401 Unauthorized` ([validated by: refuses to create a chat](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L214)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:27:- Reading a chat is refused the same way ([validated by: refuses to read a chat](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L222)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:28:- A message is refused and the orchestrator is never invoked, so an unauthenticated request costs no model call ([validated by: refuses to post a message, and never reaches the orchestrator](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L230)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:29:- The `401` precedes the chat lookup, so an unauthenticated caller cannot probe which ids exist ([validated by: answers 401 before 404, so an unauthenticated caller cannot probe which chat ids exist](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L242)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:35:- Middleware that runs but attaches no `user` is refused `401`, and the chat it asked for is not revealed ([validated by: refuses a request whose middleware attached no user, without revealing the chat](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L94)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:36:- A `user` carrying no `id` is refused ([validated by: refuses a user carrying no id](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L273)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:37:- A `null` id is refused ([validated by: refuses a null id](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L281)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:38:- An empty-string id is refused ([validated by: refuses an empty-string id](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L265)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:39:- The numeric id `0` is accepted: `id` is `string | number`, so `0` is a legal id even though it is falsy, and the check is by type and emptiness rather than by truthiness ([validated by: accepts the numeric id 0, which is falsy but legal](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L256)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:40:- A refused caller leaves nothing behind - no chat is recorded for it ([validated by: never records a chat for a caller it refused](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L289)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:46:- A request refused because no middleware is configured emits exactly one `warn` on category `http` ([validated by: emits exactly one warn on category http when no middleware is configured](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L327)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:47:- A request refused because the middleware attached no usable user emits exactly one ([validated by: emits exactly one warn when the middleware attaches no usable user](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L340)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:48:- Nothing request-derived appears in the emitted data ([validated by: records nothing derived from the request, so a refusal cannot leak what was asked for](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L348)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:49:- An authorised request emits no warning at all, so the line means a refusal rather than traffic ([validated by: says nothing at all when the request is authorised](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L356)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:55:- A created chat is answered `201` with a body carrying exactly `id` and `createdAt`, which is the pair a client destructures ([validated by: answers 201 with exactly an id and a createdAt](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L115)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:56:- The creating user's `workspaceId` is stored on the chat and reaches the orchestrator on the next message, two requests later ([validated by: carries the creating user workspace through to the orchestrator](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L127)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:62:- With no `authMiddleware`, `POST /hal/chats` is refused ([validated by: refuses to create a chat](../../src/transport/createApp.test.ts#L31)).
specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:63:- Health still answers `200` alongside that refusal ([validated by: still answers health, so a denied chat route is not a broken app](../../src/transport/createApp.test.ts#L38)).

specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:89:- A message to an id with no chat is `404`, by the same lookup-first order ([validated by: answers 404 when the chat a message names does not exist](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L164)).

specs/hal-engine-chat-routes/spec.md:92:- A refused message is not recorded, so the owner's next read shows no trace of it ([validated by: does not record the rejected message in the chat](../../src/transport/routes/chats.test.ts#L191)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:12:- `beforeToolCall?: (session: ChatSession, call: ToolCall) => Promise<ToolResponse | undefined>` is an optional member of `OrchestratorHooks`, and `ToolCall` and `ToolResponse` are importable from the package root beside it, as `example/full-config.ts` does under `npm run typecheck:example` ([validated by: hands the executor the very object the model produced when the policy returns undefined](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L109)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:13:- With no `beforeToolCall` configured, each pending call runs exactly once through the registry, as before ([validated by: runs each pending call exactly once in a two-tool round when no policy is configured](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L99)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:14:- `undefined` means proceed: the executor runs and receives the same input object the model produced, with no defensive copy between the hook and the executor ([validated by: hands the executor the very object the model produced when the policy returns undefined](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L109)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:18:- A returned `ToolResponse` declines the call: the executor never runs, and `response.result` reaches the model as the `tool_result` whose `toolUseId` is the declined call's id ([validated by: answers a declined call with the policy's result under its own id and never runs the executor](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L119)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:19:- In a round where one call is declined and another proceeds, the model receives a `tool_result` for both, in the order of the `tool_use` blocks ([validated by: answers both calls of a round where one is declined and one proceeds, in order](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L130)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:20:- A declined response takes the executor's path in full: its `clientMessages` reach the browser with an assigned entry index, the run still ends in `stream_end`, and the next user message on the same socket is answered ([validated by: delivers a declined response's client messages to the browser, then answers the next message](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L196)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:21:- A declined response with `suppressAssistantResponse: true` suppresses exactly as a tool's would, with one `suppress_output` chunk ([validated by: suppresses on a declined response that asks for it, exactly as a tool would](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L143)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:22:- The wording of a declined result belongs to the consumer; the engine only carries it ([validated by: answers a declined call with the policy's result under its own id and never runs the executor](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L119)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:26:- The hook fires only for a tool name the registry has, so a call to an unknown tool is never presented to the policy and keeps the registry's own unknown-tool path ([validated by: never consults the policy for a tool the registry does not have](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L160)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:27:- It fires once per requested call per round, not once per turn: one tool in each of three rounds is three calls, and two tools in one round is two ([validated by: consults the policy once per requested call per round across three rounds](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L219), [validated by: consults the policy once for each call of a two-tool round](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L229)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:28:- Calls within a round are presented concurrently, inside the round's existing `Promise.all`, with no ordering guarantee between them ([validated by: consults the policy once for each call of a two-tool round](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L229)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:32:- A throwing policy declines its call rather than ending the conversation: the executor does not run, the model receives a `tool_result` naming the tool, `stream_end` is sent, `afterModelResponse` fires once, and `onError` does not fire, because the turn did not fail ([validated by: declines the call when the policy throws, and the turn survives with every hook but onError](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L175)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:33:- Every `tool_use` block the provider was sent must be answered by a `tool_result`, so a raw throw escaping the round would leave the conversation unanswerable; catching it keeps the turn alive ([validated by: declines the call when the policy throws, and the turn survives with every hook but onError](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L175)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:37:- **GDPR.** The engine adds no log line carrying a value from the tool input, for a declined or an allowed call; the throw path logs the tool name and the error's type only ([validated by: writes no value from the tool input to any log line, for a declined and an allowed call](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L238)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:38:- **GDPR.** The hook receives the model's raw tool input and, through `session`, the caller's `authHeaders`; the TSDoc says so, and a policy that logs either is logging personal data and credential material ([validated by: hands the executor the very object the model produced when the policy returns undefined](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L109)).
specs/hal-engine-before-tool-call-hook/spec.md:39:- **EU AI Act, Article 14.** The TSDoc names this hook as the supported seam for a human-oversight control and points at `docs/adding-a-tool.md` for what a declined call looks like to the model; the engine asserts nothing about any policy installed through it ([validated by: answers a declined call with the policy's result under its own id and never runs the executor](../../src/transport/ws/beforeToolCall.test.ts#L119)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:8:A `([validated by](../../src/X.test.ts#Lnn))` link counts as coverage only when it sits in its statement's trailing parenthetical. The coverage job reports every other test link as `non-trailing-link` and drops it, so a spec can read as fully cited while the coverage graph records nothing. `npm run check:spec-links` is the local counterpart of that job: it segments each spec exactly as Lore does and reports every test link that falls outside a trailing parenthetical. The convention it enforces is published in AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links.
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:14:- A citation mid-way through a list item is misplaced, and each one is reported separately against the item's own first line ([validated by: a list item with two mid-item citations reports both at the item's line](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L37)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:15:- A citation mid-way through a paragraph sentence is misplaced, and is reported against the line the paragraph starts on, not the line the link sits on ([validated by: a mid-sentence citation in a paragraph reports one finding at the paragraph's line](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L44)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:16:- A citation closing its sentence is where the rule wants it and is never reported ([validated by: a paragraph sentence whose citation is trailing reports nothing](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L61)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:17:- A mid-sentence link to something other than a test file - a script, a doc - is prose, not a miscited test, and is never reported ([validated by: a mid-sentence link to a script rather than a test reports nothing](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L65)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:18:- A citation written inside backticks is documentation of the convention rather than a use of it, and is never reported ([validated by: a citation written inside backticks reports nothing](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L69)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:29:- With no path arguments it scans every `specs/<slug>/spec.md` in sorted slug order followed by `.specify/spec.md`, which is exactly the list an explicit invocation of those paths produces ([validated by: no spec paths scans the sorted specs directories plus .specify/spec.md](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L141)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:30:- Each finding prints one line carrying the spec, the statement's line, the cited path with its `#L` anchor, and the words `cited outside the statement's trailing parenthetical` ([validated by: a spec with misplaced citations exits 1 and summarises findings, specs and statements](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L79)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:31:- A citation written with no `#L` anchor prints the path alone ([validated by: a citation with no #L anchor is reported with the path alone](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L55)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:32:- The run closes with `misplaced: <N> across <M> specs (<S> statements scanned)` and exits 1 when `N` is above zero ([validated by: a spec with misplaced citations exits 1 and summarises findings, specs and statements](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L79)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:33:- A spec whose citations all sit in trailing parentheticals exits 0 under the same summary line ([validated by: a spec citing only in trailing parentheticals exits 0 with a zero summary](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L73)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:34:- `--json` replaces the report with an array alone, each entry carrying `spec`, `line`, `path`, `anchorLine`, `label` and `statement` ([validated by: --json prints only an array of findings carrying every reported field](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L88)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:35:- An unrecognised flag exits 2 with the usage line rather than scanning anything ([validated by: an unknown flag exits 2 with the usage line](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L104)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:36:- A spec path that cannot be read exits 2 naming that path, so a typo is never reported as a clean run ([validated by: a spec path that cannot be read exits 2 naming the path](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L118)).
specs/hal-engine-spec-link-placement/spec.md:40:- A relative path means the same spec from any working directory ([validated by: a relative spec path resolves against the repo root, not the working directory](../../scripts/check-spec-links.test.ts#L127)).
